assessment.title: H524 Week 3: Probability Distributions and Sampling

material.mattext:
Question 1: Binomial Conditions (5 points)

A pharmaceutical company claims that their new medication is effective for 80% of patients. Which statement BEST describes why treating 15 patients constitutes a binomial experiment?
Each patient has two outcomes (success/failure), probability stays constant at 0.80, trials are independent, and there are a fixed number (15) of trials
Each patient can have multiple outcomes, the probability changes with each patient, trials depend on previous results, and sample size is variable
The medication works most of the time, some patients get better, the trials happen sequentially, and n=15
Each patient is tested once, the success rate is high, patients don't affect each other, and we count total successes

Question 2: Binomial Probability - Exactly 12 Successes (3 points)

For the medication scenario (n=15, p=0.80), what is the probability that exactly 12 patients respond successfully?

Question 3: Binomial Probability - At Least 13 Successes (3 points)

For the same scenario, what is the probability that at least 13 patients respond successfully?

Question 4: R Code for Binomial (2 points)

Which R code correctly calculates Pr(X ≥ 13) for n=15, p=0.80?
sum(dbinom(13:15, 15, 0.80)) or pbinom(12, 15, 0.80, lower.tail=FALSE)

Question 5: Binomial Expected Value (2 points)

For the binomial scenario above (n=15, p=0.80), what is the expected number of successful responses?

Question 6: Binomial Standard Deviation (2 points)

What is the standard deviation for this binomial distribution?

Question 7: Vaccine Efficacy - Lower Tail (3 points)

A vaccine has 90% efficacy. A clinic vaccinates 25 people. What is the probability that fewer than 20 people are protected?

Question 8: Vaccine Efficacy - Range (3 points)

For the same scenario, what is the probability that between 22 and 24 people (inclusive) are protected?

Question 9: Z-Score Calculation (2 points)

Adult heights are normally distributed with mean 170 cm and standard deviation 10 cm. What is the Z-score for a person who is 185 cm tall?

Question 10: Upper Tail Probability (3 points)

Using the same height distribution, what proportion of adults are taller than 185 cm?

Question 11: Probability Between Two Values (3 points)

What proportion of adults have heights between 165 cm and 180 cm?

Question 12: 90th Percentile (3 points)

Using the height distribution (mean 170 cm, SD 10 cm), what height represents the 90th percentile?

Question 13: Manual CI Calculation (10 points)

A study measures pain reduction scores for 20 patients receiving a new treatment:

Sample mean: x̄ = 6.2 points
Sample standard deviation: s = 2.4 points
Sample size: n = 20

  1. Should you use a z or t distribution? Why? (2 points)
  2. Find the appropriate critical value for a 95% confidence interval. (2 points)
  3. Calculate the standard error. (2 points)
  4. Calculate the margin of error. (2 points)
  5. Construct the 95% confidence interval. (2 points)

Question 14: 25th Percentile (2 points)

What height represents the 25th percentile?

Question 15: CI with R (5 points)

A clinical trial measures cholesterol reduction for 30 patients:

cholesterol_reduction <- c(28, 32, 25, 30, 27, 35, 22, 29, 31, 26,
24, 33, 28, 30, 27, 29, 31, 25, 28, 32,
26, 30, 29, 27, 34, 28, 31, 25, 29, 30)
  1. Write R code to calculate a 95% confidence interval using t.test(). (2 points)
  2. Report the confidence interval. (1 point)
  3. Based on this interval, is there strong evidence that the mean reduction exceeds 25 mg/dL? Explain. (2 points)

Question 16: Empirical Rule Range (2 points)

Cholesterol levels are normally distributed with mean 200 mg/dL and SD 40 mg/dL. Using the empirical rule, within what range do approximately 95% of cholesterol values fall?
120 to 280 mg/dL
160 to 240 mg/dL
180 to 220 mg/dL
100 to 300 mg/dL

Question 17: Extreme Cholesterol Values (3 points)

What proportion have cholesterol levels above 280 mg/dL?

Question 18: Hypertension Proportion (2 points)

Systolic blood pressure is normally distributed with mean 125 mmHg and SD 18 mmHg. What proportion have blood pressure above 140 mmHg (hypertension)?

Question 19: Expected Number Hypertensive (2 points)

If 1000 people are screened, approximately how many would be classified as hypertensive?

Question 20: Sampling Distribution Mean (2 points)

A population has mean μ = 100 and standard deviation σ = 20. If you take a sample of size n=25, what is the mean of the sampling distribution of X̄?

Question 21: Standard Error Calculation (2 points)

What is the standard error of X̄ for n=25?

item.title: Question 22: Effect of Sample Size on SE

material.mattext:
Question 22: Effect of Sample Size on SE (3 points)

If n=100 instead of n=25, what is the new standard error?

Question 23: CLT Distribution (2 points)

A population of glucose levels has mean 100 mg/dL and standard deviation 25 mg/dL. A sample of 64 individuals is randomly selected. According to the Central Limit Theorem, the sample mean X̄ is distributed as:

item.title: Question 24: Sample Mean Probability - Upper Tail

material.mattext:
Question 24: Sample Mean Probability - Upper Tail (4 points)

For the glucose scenario above, what is the probability that the sample mean exceeds 105 mg/dL?

Question 25: Sample Mean Probability - Range (2 points)

What is the probability that the sample mean glucose level is between 97 and 103 mg/dL?

Question 26: SD vs SE Calculation (2 points)

If the population standard deviation is 30 and sample size is 36, what is the standard error?

item.title: Question 27: Effect of Sample Size on SE

material.mattext:
Question 27: Effect of Sample Size on SE (2 points)

As sample size increases, what happens to the standard error and why is this important?
SE decreases; this makes our estimates more precise and reliable for inference
SE increases; this makes our estimates more conservative
SE stays the same; sample size doesn't affect variability
SE decreases; this makes the population standard deviation smaller

Question 28: SD vs SE Concept (1 point)

What is the key difference between standard deviation (SD) and standard error (SE)?
SD measures variability of individual observations; SE measures variability of sample means
SD measures variability of sample means; SE measures variability of individual observations
SD is always larger than SE
SD and SE are the same when n=1

Question 29: CLT Birth Weight Probability (3 points)

Birth weights have mean 3400g and SD 500g. You sample 100 births. What is the probability that the sample mean birth weight is less than 3350g?

Question 30: R Code for CLT (2 points)

Which R code correctly calculates the probability in Question 29?
pnorm(3350, 3400, 50, lower.tail=FALSE)

Question 31: CI Interpretation (2 points)

Based on Question 13, which statement correctly interprets the 95% confidence interval for mean pain reduction?
We are 95% confident that the true mean pain reduction for all patients receiving this treatment is between 5.08 and 7.32 points
95% of patients will have pain reduction between 5.08 and 7.32 points
There is a 95% probability that the sample mean is between 5.08 and 7.32 points
The population mean is definitely between 5.08 and 7.32 points with 95% certainty

Question 32: Meaning of 95% Confidence (2 points)

What does "95% confident" mean in the context of confidence intervals?
If we repeated this study many times, 95% of the confidence intervals we construct would contain the true population mean
95% of the data values fall within the confidence interval
There is a 95% probability that our specific interval contains the population mean
We are 95% sure our sample mean equals the population mean

Question 33: Comparing Confidence Levels (1 point)

If you calculated a 99% confidence interval instead of 95%, the interval would be:
Wider, because we need a larger range to be more confident we've captured the true mean
Narrower, because we are more confident about the estimate
The same width, confidence level doesn't affect interval width
Wider, but only if sample size increases

Question 34: Comprehensive Problem (5 points)

A pharmaceutical company tests a new drug. In trials with 80 patients:

  • 72 patients respond successfully
  • Mean cholesterol reduction: x̄ = 35 mg/dL
  • Standard deviation: s = 8 mg/dL
  1. Calculate a 95% confidence interval for the true success rate (proportion). Hint: For proportions, use p̂ ± 1.96√(p̂(1-p̂)/n) (2 points)
  2. Calculate a 95% confidence interval for the true mean cholesterol reduction. (2 points)
  3. Write complete R code to perform both calculations and create a visualization of the cholesterol reduction data. (1 point)

Question 35: AI Verification and Learning (5 bonus points)

Choose ONE problem from Part 3 (Sampling Distributions and CLT).

  1. Ask an AI tool (Claude, ChatGPT, etc.) to solve the problem. Include your exact prompt. (1 point)
  2. Verify the AI's answer by working through it yourself step-by-step. Did the AI get it correct? If not, identify the error. (2 points)
  3. Ask the AI to explain the Central Limit Theorem using a medical example different from those in class. Evaluate the quality of the explanation. (2 points)
